Draw a closed diagram to decompose it.

What this is

An edge of D, read as a 4-valent plane graph, is nonalternating when the strand is the overstrand at both of its ends, or the understrand at both. Mark every such edge with two points and, inside each face, join the marked points that are adjacent along the boundary without lying on the same edge. Those arcs close up into disjoint simple closed curves that cut the sphere into maximal alternating regions.

The alternating decomposition graph G has one vertex per curve and one edge per nonalternating edge of D, and an alternating diagram gives a single vertex with no edges. G is always planar and bipartite with every vertex of even degree, and it determines the Turaev surface: gT(G) above is computed from the abstract graph by the recursion of Corollary 3.9, with no reference to the diagram, and must agree with the gT(D) read off the all-A and all-B states at the top of this panel.

Method: Armond and Lowrance, “Turaev genus and alternating decompositions”, Algebr. Geom. Topol. 17 (2017) 793–830.

Diagram actions

Make alternating switches the fewest crossings on closed components; it can change the knot type.

Definitions & limits

Matching invariants do not prove equivalence. The determinant is shown for a single-component knot. Fox colorings include the three constant colorings; “nonconstant” means at least two colors are used. Coloring and determinant calculations support up to 200 crossings.

Jones uses V(unknot) = 1 and V(t) = (−A³)−w(D)⟨D⟩ with A = t−1/4. Exact state expansion supports up to 18 crossings. Link polynomials may have half-integer powers.

Methods: Kauffman: Jones polynomial; Kolay: coloring matrices; linking numbers.

No batch results.

Definitions & research limits

A block is homogeneous when all its crossing edges have one sign. Different blocks may have opposite signs. A failed diagram test does not rule out another homogeneous diagram of the same knot or link.

Canonical genus belongs to this diagram. For a homogeneous knot diagram, the Seifert surface has minimal genus. Disconnected surfaces display the sum of their genera.

V(t) = 1 is an exact polynomial test, not an unknot certificate. Circle IDs follow crossing IDs and smoothing branches within this diagram; they are not knot invariants.

References: Cromwell · Manchón · Research guide & dataset formats

Dragging

30

Drag radius and Pass underneath are in the Drag strand tool's options bar below the canvas. Hold Shift while dragging to reverse underneath for that gesture. Only real topology (Reidemeister validity) gates a move — while the gesture is in progress crossings are free to pass arbitrarily close together, or briefly overlap, as long as the move is valid; separating them, if at all, happens once on release. A strand still cannot be pulled through another strand: every crossing that appears or disappears has to be a genuine R1 or R2, so dragging can never change the knot.

Controls & shortcuts

Draw Turn Auto-close off for open arcs. Joining an endpoint passes under existing arcs.

Drag Move strands with Reidemeister moves. + and − change the drag radius from any tool. Drag empty space to pan; pinch or scroll to zoom.

Erase “Erase strand” removes one strand between crossings or endpoints; “Erase segment” rubs out just what the cursor covers; “Erase curve” takes the whole curve you tap, which is how you remove one component of a link. E cycles the three. “Clear all” empties the diagram in one undo step.

Lasso Select whole curves or a region. Drag to move; use the round handle to rotate.

Smoothing “Smooth corners” applies to new pen strokes, and takes up the slack around the grip while dragging, so pulling on an already-stretched strand draws it back in. “Smooth sharp corners” edits existing curves, and also runs automatically when a drag ends; Auto-relax spreads the diagram.

Lasso Enclose curves to select them, or switch the shape to Rectangle and just drag a box. Drag inside the box to move it, the corner grip to resize, and the handle above it to rotate. Auto-relax slowly shrinks a diagram, so the grip is how you bring it back up to a comfortable working size.

Crossing overlap “Separate overlapping crossings” (Settings) eases apart any crossings a drag pushed into each other, once the drag ends, and turns them back open so the strands meet at a readable angle. “Separation distance” sets how far. Crossings that were already close stay put.

D Draw · E Erase · L Lasso · V Drag · X Switch crossing · A Auto-relax · F Full screen · + / − Drag radius · 1–4 Views
